parsed.draft_response:
Thanks for reporting this, and we agree this should be treated as high priority. We can confirm we’ll escalate to our Security team for investigation.

At this stage, we understand the behavior you observed: a report link created in one workspace may be visible/accessible from another workspace if the URL is forwarded. You’ve noted that data exfiltration hasn’t been confirmed, so our initial focus is to determine what an unauthorized workspace can actually access (the link/metadata versus the underlying report data) and how tenant/workspace access is validated for forwarded URLs.

To help Security investigate quickly, could you share the following minimum details?
1) Product/feature name involved (and where the “report link” is generated from)
2) Steps to reproduce (including any specific roles/permissions for both the sending and receiving users)
3) What happens on the receiving side: can they view the full report, any data, or only see the link/landing page?
4) Whether you can provide example URLs (redacted as needed) and the workspace/tenant identifiers involved (or timestamps and approximate tenant/workspace names)
5) Any relevant time window and whether you observed repeated attempts or successful access
6) Any logs/telemetry you may have (e.g., audit events showing the receiving user accessed the report)

In the meantime, if you have the ability to do so in your environment, please avoid further forwarding or sharing of the affected links beyond what’s necessary for your internal validation, to reduce any potential exposure while we investigate.
promised_actions: Escalate the report to our Security team for investigation
safety_notes: We have not confirmed data exfiltration or verified cross-tenant impact; avoid asserting a security vulnerability or root cause.
Request minimum reproduction details and authentication/authorization behavior to support Security’s investigation.
Advise caution about further sharing without promising containment or immediate remediation.
